title: Budget Tracker
story: Paycheck comes in, bills go out, $4.75 for coffee, $12.99 for lunch. Where does the money go? A budget tracker that records income and expenses, categorizes them, and shows your balance — the financial awareness app in 100 lines of code.
why: A budget tracker combines structs for transactions, Vec for history, enums for categories, and running balance calculation — practical personal finance in code.
analogy: A checkbook register where you write every deposit and withdrawal, maintaining a running balance. Your budget tracker is the digital register: income adds to the balance column, expenses subtract, and categories let you see WHERE the money goes. The report is your monthly statement.
try_it: Add budget limits per category — warn when spending exceeds a category budget. Add recurring transactions (monthly rent, weekly groceries). Implement a savings goal tracker. Add date tracking to transactions and show monthly reports.
tips: Track income and expenses separately — income_total and expense_total
Balance = income_total - expense_total at all times
Categories help answer 'where did my money go?' — essential insight
common_mistakes: Subtracting expenses from balance but not adding to expense_total — double bookkeeping
Not handling overdraft — expenses can make balance negative
Mixing up amount signs — income is positive addition, expense is positive subtraction
